backlog.spec: Supply the gradient of the objective (-sum of radii) and the Jacobian of the constraint vector cons(v) to scipy.minimize via the jac argument of the constraint dict and the minimize call. For each pair constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 the derivative with respect to centre i is (c_i - c_j)/d_ij and with respect to radius i is -1, with the opposite sign for j. Boundary constraints have simple unit or zero entries. Vectorise the construction with numpy index arrays. This removes finite-difference cost so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper, allowing more restarts within the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of building all n(n-1)/2 = 325 pair-overlap constraints every iteration, only include pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold (for example 0.35) at the start of each SLSQP call. Build the active pair list once from the initial centres, then pass only those pairs into cons. Re-check after the optimisation finishes: if any excluded pair now overlaps, add it and re-run SLSQP from the result. This shrinks the constraint matrix and speeds up each SLSQP step.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the proportional pairwise shrinking in _repair with an exact optimisation of radii for the fixed centres. Solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i), with r >= 0. The LP gives the largest feasible radii for those centres, so the repaired sum is never worse than the current heuristic. Subtract a tiny margin (about 1e-12) before returning so the double-precision check passes.
backlog.title: Exact LP repair for fixed centres

backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP solve, keep the best packing found so far. For each subsequent iteration, copy the best centres and radii, add Gaussian noise to the centres (sigma about 0.03), and re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept the new packing only if its repaired radius sum is larger than the incumbent. Use the remaining time budget entirely on this local perturbation loop rather than on fresh uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Monotonic basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: From the current best packing, pick the circle with the smallest radius (or a random one among the smallest three), delete it, and search for the largest empty spot in the unit square by evaluating a 60x60 grid of candidate points and taking the one maximising the minimum distance to other centres and to the walls. Place the circle there with a small radius, then run SLSQP on the full configuration. Accept the move only if the repaired sum improves. This is a structured perturbation that targets wasted space.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle move

backlog.spec: Within the basin-hopping loop, choose a random pair of circles with clearly different radii and swap their centre positions while keeping the radii attached to their original indices, then re-optimise with SLSQP. Circles near the centre of the square generally have larger radii in good packings, so the swap explores different size-to-location assignments. Accept only strict improvements of the repaired radius sum.
backlog.title: Swap move between large and small circles

backlog.spec: Before calling SLSQP, relax the packing with L-BFGS-B on an energy that combines -sum(r) with a quadratic penalty on squared overlaps and wall violations, scaled by a weight that is increased geometrically over several rounds (for example 10, 100, 1000, 10000). This drives centres into a near-feasible configuration with a smooth landscape. Then polish with SLSQP starting from that configuration, which typically needs fewer iterations.
backlog.title: Penalty-method pre-relaxation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Generate a pool of random starts and run a short SLSQP (for example maxiter 40) on each. Keep only the best quarter by repaired radius sum, then continue optimising those survivors to full convergence with a larger iteration cap. Repeat with a shrinking pool if time remains. This spends little time on hopeless starts and concentrates CPU on promising basins.
backlog.title: Successive halving over random starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, track the number of consecutive rejected perturbations. Start with a Gaussian centre perturbation sigma of 0.02. Each time 10 perturbations in a row fail to improve the incumbent, multiply sigma by 1.5 (capped at 0.2); each time a perturbation improves, reset sigma to 0.02. This lets the search take small local steps when near a good optimum and larger jumps when it is stuck.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation strength

backlog.spec: Divide the 24 s CPU budget into two phases. For the first 40 percent, run fresh uniform random restarts as in the current script and keep the best. For the remaining 60 percent, run basin hopping only around that best packing with small perturbations. The fraction is a fixed constant. This combines broad coverage at the start with intensive refinement at the end.
backlog.title: Time-scheduled switch from exploration to exploitation

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 and pass options ftol of about 1e-12 to SLSQP so the optimiser actually converges to the local maximum instead of stopping early. Check res.success and, if it is false, keep the result only if it is still feasible after repair. These settings alone let each local solve reach a tighter local optimum.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration cap and tighten tolerance

backlog.spec: Replace the global clip of centres to [0,1] with a clip to [r, 1-r] per circle before repair, so that boundary circles are not initially pushed through walls. Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12, and in _repair use a final pass that enforces every constraint with a tolerance well under 1e-10. The aim is to recover the small amount of radius sum lost to the safety margin and to clipping artifacts.
backlog.title: Shrink margin and boundary clipping tuning

backlog.spec: Some random restarts are seeded from a hexagonal-like lattice: generate a grid of points with spacing chosen so that about 26 to 32 points fit in the square, select 26 of them at random (or drop extras), then jitter each centre by Gaussian noise of sigma 0.02 using the seeded rng. Use these lattice starts for roughly half the restarts and uniform random starts for the rest. Lattice configurations are often close to good packings for this n.
backlog.title: Hexagonal lattice seeded starts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres with a scrambled Halton or Sobol-style sequence generated from the seed, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Low-discrepancy starts cover the square more evenly, which can reduce the number of restarts needed to reach a good basin. Keep the initial radii at INIT_RADIUS. Everything else in the restart loop stays the same.
backlog.title: Low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to 0.05, set each initial radius from the nearest-neighbour distance of the initial centres: r_i = 0.5 * min_j |c_i - c_j| * U, where U is uniform in [0.6, 0.9] drawn from the seeded rng, and also capped by the distance to the nearest wall. A feasible-ish starting point lets SLSQP begin close to a valid packing, which typically leads to a better local optimum.
backlog.title: Radius-aware initial radii

backlog.spec: Draw the initial radii from a heavy-tailed distribution (for example the absolute value of a normal with scale 0.08, clipped to [0.01, 0.2]) rather than a constant. Varied starting sizes push the optimiser into a wider set of size hierarchies, which matters because good packings for this problem mix large and small circles. Keep the rest of the restart loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Random radius size distribution at start

backlog.spec: For each restart, after computing a packing, apply one of the eight symmetries of the square (rotations by 90 degrees and reflections) chosen by the rng. This does not change the radius sum but gives a canonical comparison and is not needed for scoring. Instead, use the symmetries as an additional diversification step: before a basin-hopping perturbation, apply a random symmetry to the incumbent so that perturbations act on different sides of the packing.
backlog.title: Symmetry-breaking random orientation of the square

backlog.spec: Maintain a pool of the best 5 distinct packings found so far, where distinct means their sorted radii differ by more than 1e-3 in L2 norm. Each iteration, choose a random pool member (biased toward better ones), perturb its centres with Gaussian noise, re-optimise with SLSQP, and insert the result into the pool if it qualifies. Return the best member at the end. The pool keeps several basins alive rather than one.
backlog.title: Elite pool with diversity

backlog.spec: Maintain a small population of good packings. To create a child, take the centres of circles on the left half of parent A and the right half of parent B, fill any count mismatch with random points, and then run SLSQP. Accept the child into the population if it beats the worst member and is not a duplicate. This crossover-like operator mixes good local structures from different basins.
backlog.title: Population-based recombination of packings

backlog.spec: Alternate between two subproblems: first fix the radii and optimise only the centres to maximise feasibility margin (minimise the maximum pairwise overlap penalty), then fix the centres and solve the exact radius LP as in the repair step. Repeat a few rounds from each start. Separating the two steps can make the landscape easier for each individual solver, especially for the centre placement.
backlog.title: Hierarchical alternating optimisation

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP for the final polish with a custom log-barrier method: maximise sum(r) + mu * sum(log(slack)) over all pair and wall slacks, using scipy.optimize.minimize with method 'BFGS' or 'L-BFGS-B' and an analytic gradient. Decrease mu geometrically from 1e-1 to 1e-7. Slacks stay strictly positive, so every iterate is feasible, which removes the need for an explicit repair in most cases.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior point on the radius sum

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision variables and constraints so they are of order one. For instance, optimise centres in the unit square and radii multiplied by 10, and divide the pair constraints by 0.1. Well-conditioned constraints help SLSQP's quasi-Newton approximation of the Lagrangian converge in fewer iterations. Undo the scaling before returning the centres and radii.
backlog.title: Constraint and variable scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each local SLSQP solve, add small multiplicative noise to all radii (for example a factor in [0.97, 1.03]) and run SLSQP once more from that point before repair. This acts as a regulariser that lets the optimiser escape flat or nearly degenerate local optima where some circles are stuck at tiny radii. Keep the result only if the repaired radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Noise injection on radii during restarts

backlog.spec: Add a small regularisation term lambda * sum((r_i - mean(r))^2) with lambda around 1e-3 to the SLSQP objective for the first solve in each restart, then solve again with lambda set to zero from that point. The shaping term pulls the optimiser toward more uniform radii first, which often gives a smoother path to a good configuration. The final solve uses the true objective.
backlog.title: Penalise radius variance as a shaping term

backlog.spec: After a local solve, detect circles whose radius is below 0.3 times the mean radius. Remove them, re-run SLSQP for the remaining circles with n reduced, then re-insert each removed circle into the largest empty spot found by grid search over the square and run a final SLSQP on all n. This targets the frequent local optimum with a stuck tiny circle.
backlog.title: Random removal of tiny circles

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, accept a new packing even when its repaired sum is slightly lower than the incumbent, with probability exp(-(old - new)/T), where T starts at 0.01 and decays linearly to 0 over the time budget. Always keep a separate record of the best packing seen. This simulated-annealing-style acceptance helps the search cross barriers between basins.
backlog.title: Stochastic acceptance of worse packings

backlog.spec: Measure the average CPU time of a single SLSQP local solve during the first two restarts and use that to decide how many local solves to run in total, reserving the final 5 percent of the budget for a repair and validation pass. Stop early if the time budget would be exceeded. This avoids wasted budget at the end and makes the loop adapt to machine speed rather than relying on a fixed TIME_FRACTION.
backlog.title: Time-aware restart budget by n

backlog.spec: For each random start, compute a cheap score: run only 20 SLSQP iterations and compute the repaired radius sum. Run the full SLSQP only on the top 20 percent of starts by this proxy score. This lets the search evaluate many more starting points per second while still refining the promising ones to convergence.
backlog.title: Two-stage restart selection with cheap proxy

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, generate a batch of 8 perturbed candidates from the incumbent with different random noise levels, run the cheap 30-iteration SLSQP on each, and fully optimise only the single best candidate by proxy score. Compared with one full solve per perturbation, this evaluates more candidate moves for the same CPU time.
backlog.title: Batch evaluation of perturbation candidates

backlog.spec: Perturb the incumbent by re-initialising a random subset of 3 to 6 circles uniformly in the square, keeping the rest of the packing intact, then run SLSQP. Partial re-initialisation is a larger but more structured move than adding global Gaussian noise, and it preserves good structure in the unchanged circles.
backlog.title: Gaussian centre noise plus per-circle random restarts

backlog.spec: Keep the best packing found so far. Before each restart, with probability 0.5, instead of a uniform random start, take the best packing and apply one of the 8 symmetries of the square (identity, 3 rotations, 4 reflections: (x,y)->(1-x,y), (y,x), etc.) chosen at random with rng, then add Gaussian noise of scale 0.02 to the centres and clip to [0.01, 0.99]. Radii start at INIT_RADIUS. Run the existing SLSQP and repair unchanged and keep the best result. Only the start point changes.
backlog.title: Dihedral warm starts from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Continuation in n. Inside solve, first run the existing random-restart SLSQP for n+1 circles for a fixed share (about 25 percent) of the time budget and keep its best packing. Remove the circle with the smallest radius to get n circles, use its centres and radii as the start for the remaining restarts and perturb the centres with Gaussian noise of scale 0.01. Run SLSQP and repair as before and keep the best of all candidates. The repair and output format stay the same.
backlog.title: Drop the smallest circle from an (n+1) packing

backlog.spec: Restrict a fraction of restarts to packings symmetric under reflection about the vertical line x = 0.5 (or the diagonal y = x, chosen by rng). Parameterise only the free circles: for n circles, pair them into mirror pairs plus circles on the axis, so the optimiser variables are half the size. Build the full (n, 2) centres and (n,) radii from these variables, run SLSQP on the reduced problem with the same constraints, then expand and call the existing repair. Keep the unrestricted restarts too, and return the best valid packing over both families.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric reduced search

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, repeatedly pick a random axis-aligned window (a square of side 0.35 to 0.5 in the unit square, chosen with rng). Freeze all circles whose centres lie outside the window, keeping their centres and radii fixed. Re-optimise the centres and radii of circles inside the window with SLSQP, with constraints against all circles including the frozen ones. Accept the new packing only if the sum of radii increases, then run the repair step. Each iteration is one SLSQP call on a small subset of variables, so many iterations fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-optimisation of a window

backlog.spec: Build a start packing without random positions. Place circles one at a time: sample about 2000 candidate points uniformly in the square with rng, and place each new circle at the candidate with the largest distance to the nearest existing centre and to the boundary, with its radius set to that clearance times 0.9. Repeat for all n circles to get a feasible greedy packing. Use it as the SLSQP start in one restart, and use random starts for the rest. Keep the best valid result as before.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole constructive start

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP run, spread the random initial centres apart. Run about 30 iterations of a Lloyd relaxation: for each point, compute a repulsion vector from its nearest-neighbour distances with a weight 1/d^2 summed over all other centres, move each centre by 0.02 times the normalised sum, and clip to [0.05, 0.95]. Then assign INIT_RADIUS and call the existing SLSQP and repair. This changes only the initial positions and keeps the optimiser unchanged.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style spreading before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, change the SLSQP objective to minus the radius sum minus a bonus lam * sum(log(r + 1e-6)) with lam starting at 0.01 and decaying linearly to 0 over two passes of SLSQP. Run the first pass with the regularised objective, then run a second SLSQP pass from its output with the plain objective (-sum r). The log term keeps radii from collapsing early and helps the optimiser move between basins. Keep the constraints, the repair, and the best-of-restarts selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Entropy-regularised radius objective annealed to zero

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, run one extra SLSQP polish on it. Identify the active pairs, meaning pairs whose gap is below 1e-6, and the active wall constraints, and keep only those constraints (plus all pairs with gap below 0.05). Optimise centres and radii from the repaired state with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-12. Repair the result again, and return it only if its radius sum is larger than before. This recovers radius slack lost in the heuristic repair.
backlog.title: Active-set polish after repair

backlog.spec: Replace the single joint SLSQP call in each restart with alternating blocks. Round 1: fix the radii and optimise the centres with SLSQP to maximise the minimum slack (all pair gaps and wall gaps) using a single slack variable t. Round 2: fix the centres and maximise the radius sum with a linear program or SLSQP on the radii only. Repeat the two rounds three times, then run the usual joint SLSQP from the final state with maxiter 100. Keep the repair and the best-of-restarts selection.
backlog.title: Alternating block coordinate optimisation

backlog.spec: Maintain three start generators: uniform random, edge-biased (put about a third of the circles on random points along the four sides), and the dihedral warm start from the incumbent. Keep a running score for each (best radius sum it has produced so far, and the number of uses). Choose the generator for each restart with a UCB rule, using rng to break ties and a cap of 60 percent of the budget on any single generator. Run the existing SLSQP and repair for the chosen start and update its score. The output format is unchanged.
backlog.title: Bandit allocation over start strategies

backlog.spec: Replace the free 2n-coordinate search with a 180-degree rotation-symmetric one. Optimise m = n/2 free centres c_k with radii r_k, and place the partner of each centre at (1 - x, 1 - y) with the same radius, so the packing is C2-symmetric about the square's centre. For n = 26 this gives 13 free circles and 26 total. Build the SLSQP constraints on the full 26-circle set (overlap, wall, and radius >= 0) generated from the reduced vector, with maxiter as before. Run the usual restart loop, keep the best, then do one unrestricted SLSQP polish from the best symmetric packing using all 26 circles before repair. Mirror symmetry was tried before, but C2 is a different subgroup and has not been tested.
backlog.title: C2 rotational-symmetry reduced search

backlog.spec: Replace the random uniform start with a physical growth process. Begin with n points at random positions (from the seeded rng) with zero radius and random velocities. Repeat: move points by their velocities, grow all radii at a fixed rate, and when two circles or a circle and a wall touch, reflect or exchange their velocities and freeze the contact radius for that pair. Stop when the growth has jammed, or after a fixed number of events. Use the resulting centres and radii as the SLSQP start, and keep the rest of the restart loop and repair unchanged. The goal is that the physical jammed states are a different, better-spread distribution of basins than uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth start

backlog.spec: In each restart, draw a weight vector w_i from U(0.5, 1.5), one per circle, using the seeded rng. Optimise the weighted objective -sum(w_i * r_i) with the same SLSQP constraints. This steers each restart toward a different preferred size distribution, so the restarts explore different basins. Always score the candidate with the true unweighted sum of radii after repair, so the best-of selection is unchanged. Optionally resample weights every restart. The change is one line in the objective plus the weight draw.
backlog.title: Random per-restart objective weights

backlog.spec: Before the free-radii SLSQP, solve a max-min problem with a single shared radius: maximise t subject to pairwise distance >= 2t, wall distance >= t, using the random centres as the start. Then use the resulting centres with radii all set to t as the starting point for the usual SLSQP that optimises each radius separately. This two-stage schedule first finds a well-spread equal-size packing and then lets the radii differentiate. It keeps the same restart loop, repair, and seed handling.
backlog.title: Equal-radius max-min warm start

backlog.spec: After the restart loop finishes, take the best (centres, radii) and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same overlap and wall constraints, with the radii as variables and -sum(r) as the objective. Use gtol and xtol around 1e-10 and a max of 500 iterations, and budget it within the remaining time (or a fixed slice such as 5 percent of time_limit). Accept the polished result only if its radius sum is higher after repair, otherwise keep the SLSQP packing. This tests whether a different local solver finds a nearby improvement that SLSQP's stopping point misses.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Keep an archive of the best-found packings from earlier restarts. For each new SLSQP start, compute a basin signature, for example the sorted list of radii plus a coarse grid histogram of centres, and compare it to the archive. If the start is too close to an archived basin (a distance threshold), redraw the start from the rng up to a few times before using it. This forces the restarts to visit new basins rather than repeatedly landing in common ones. Keep the signature code to a few lines using numpy only.
backlog.title: Tabu on previously found basins

backlog.spec: Pass a callback to SLSQP that records the current objective and, after a warm-up of about 30 iterations, aborts the run if the current radius sum is more than a margin (for example 5 percent) below the best sum found so far. Abort by raising a private exception caught around minimize, and then use the last iterate, which is still a valid start for repair. This spends the saved time on more restarts, which the notes suggest is the more productive use of compute. It differs from successive halving because it stops individual runs within a restart rather than discarding whole starts after a fixed batch.
backlog.title: Per-iteration early abort of hopeless SLSQP runs

backlog.spec: At each restart, draw a random number of large circles from {2, 3, 4} and assign them initial radius 0.12 while the rest start at a smaller radius such as 0.07. Place the large circles first, at random positions from the rng, and the rest at random positions in the square. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same. This seeds different size hierarchies, which the best-known packings for this n appear to use, so the optimiser can start in the right hierarchy class rather than discovering it from equal small radii.
backlog.title: Tier-structured initial radii

backlog.spec: Each restart, place a random number k in {6, 7, 8} of circles on a ring along the square's boundary, spaced evenly with a random phase drawn from the rng and inset by a small margin. Fill the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior. The boundary ring is a structure that the best packings for this n show, but random starts seldom reproduce it. Use the same SLSQP, repair, and best-of selection. This is a data-side seeding change and does not touch the optimiser.
backlog.title: Angular re-seeding of the boundary ring

backlog.spec: Generate a batch of B starts (for example 40) from the rng. Run SLSQP on each with a small maxiter (for example 40) and record the radius sum. Sort the batch and run the full maxiter SLSQP only on the top 3, then repair and keep the best. Use the screening loop so that the proportion of time spent on full runs stays fixed within the time limit. Unlike the successive-halving idea, which uses fixed rounds, this is a single screen-and-refine pass per batch repeated until time is used, and it makes the batch size an explicit tuning knob.
backlog.title: Batch cheap-screen then full polish

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the sqrt pair constraint with the smooth squared form: (cx_i-cx_j)^2+(cy_i-cy_j)^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, keeping the same boundary constraints and the same pair index arrays. The square-root gradient blows up when two centres nearly coincide, so this removes that singularity and may let SLSQP converge more often within MAX_ITER. Leave _repair unchanged, so validity is still enforced exactly by the final shrink step. Keep the same restart loop and time budget.
backlog.title: Squared-distance non-overlap constraints for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call in _solve_once with an augmented Lagrangian method. Keep the variables (centres and radii) and the same constraint vector g(v) >= 0. Minimise -sum(r) + sum over constraints of multiplier-weighted penalty terms, using L-BFGS-B with box bounds [0,1] on centre coordinates and [0,0.5] on radii for the inner problem. Run about 8 outer iterations: after each inner solve, update multipliers as lambda = max(0, lambda - mu*g) and grow the penalty mu by a factor of 3. Finish with one SLSQP call from the resulting point to get the active set exact. The method is genuinely different from SLSQP alone and may escape some of its stalls.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian outer loop with L-BFGS-B inner solves

backlog.spec: Add a new start generator _mc_start(n, rng) that replaces the uniform random centres. Begin with n random centres and tiny radii. Run a hard-disk Monte Carlo loop for about 3000 sweeps: propose a random displacement of each circle by a step that adapts to keep about 40% acceptance, accept it only if the circle stays in the square and does not overlap any other circle with its current radius, and after each sweep set every radius to the largest value that keeps the packing valid, growing slowly toward the geometric maximum. Use the output centres and radii as x0 for the existing SLSQP call. The seed argument must drive all randomness through rng. This is a physically motivated compression start, not a copy of the Lubachevsky-Stillinger growth already tried, since moves are rejection-based and the radii are set by the packing itself.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo pressure compression as a start

backlog.spec: Replace the body of _repair with a global feasibility step. First clip centres into [r, 1-r] per circle. Then compute the minimum over all pairs of d_ij/(r_i+r_j) and the boundary ratios. If this minimum is below 1, scale all radii by it and additionally scale the centre offsets from (0.5,0.5) by a factor chosen so that boundary-touching circles stay inside. Repeat until no violation exceeds 1e-12, then subtract SHRINK. This keeps the relative radius profile intact instead of repeatedly cutting the pair with the largest overlap, which may recover more of the radius sum on the same centres. Keep the function signature and its return value the same.
backlog.title: Joint uniform-scale repair instead of pairwise shrinking

backlog.spec: Replace uniform random initialisation with a small evolution strategy over the start vector. Maintain a Gaussian over the 3n-vector x0 (centres and radii, with centres mapped into [0.1, 0.9] by a clip). Each generation, sample a population of 8 starts from the current mean and covariance, run the existing short SLSQP (maxiter about 60) from each, score by the repaired radius sum, and update the mean toward the top 2 and the covariance with a rank-mu update, using a fixed step size of 0.3. Restart the distribution from a fresh uniform sample when the best score has not improved for 5 generations. Use the seed for all sampling and keep the existing time budget. Spend the final 20 percent of the budget on a full-length SLSQP from the best start found.
backlog.title: CMA-ES search over initial configurations

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that builds a lattice of rows and columns, where the row count and column count are drawn at random from integers whose product is at least n, for example 5x5, 4x7, 6x5. Place the centres on a regular grid inside [0.1,0.9]^2 with an added random jitter of up to 0.3 of the grid spacing, then delete random extra nodes to leave exactly n centres. Assign initial radii of about 0.45 times the smaller grid spacing. Use this start with probability 0.5 and the existing uniform random start otherwise, selected from rng. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. This is a different structured prior from the hexagonal and tier-based starts already tried.
backlog.title: Randomised rectangular-lattice starting grids

backlog.spec: After repair, add a polish pass applied to the best packing only. For each circle i in turn, hold the others fixed and search a grid of 60 by 60 candidate positions in the square. For each candidate p, compute the largest radius that fits: the minimum of the distance to each other circle minus that circle's radius, and the distance to each wall. Move circle i to the candidate that maximises that feasible radius, but only if the new value exceeds its current radius. Also set radii to the feasible maxima after each move. Repeat over all circles for 3 passes, then run _repair once more to guarantee validity. This is a derivative-free local move that can reposition a rattler into a gap, which SLSQP rarely does.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise centre re-placement polish

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty term to the SLSQP objective: lambda times the sum of squared distances of the centres from (0.5, 0.5), with lambda set to 1e-3 for the first half of each restart's iterations and 0 after. The objective becomes -sum(r) + lambda * sum(|c_i - 0.5|^2). The idea is to stop rattlers and loose circles from drifting to the boundary, where they can be locked in and waste space and where SLSQP gradients become degenerate. Implement it by passing a modified objective and gradient to minimize, leaving the constraints unchanged. The final score is still computed as the repaired radius sum, so the penalty only guides the search.
backlog.title: Weak centre-pull regulariser to break translation degeneracy

backlog.spec: Use the full time budget more accurately. Inside _solve_once, record the process time at which the call started and the deadline TIME_FRACTION times time_limit. Wrap the constraint function so that it raises a private exception once the deadline is passed, and catch that exception in _solve_once. The salvage uses the last iterate stored by the constraint function, which is the most recent point it evaluated. Pass that point to repair and accept it only if its repaired radius sum beats the current best. This prevents a long SLSQP run from being discarded when it would have finished just past the cut-off, and avoids wasting the last seconds of budget on a call that is not started. Keep the return signature of solve unchanged.
backlog.title: Deadline-aware SLSQP with best-iterate salvage

backlog.spec: For each random start x0 drawn in _solve_once, also build its antithetic partner by mapping every centre c to (1-c_x, 1-c_y) (the point reflection through the square centre), keeping the same radii. Run SLSQP and _repair from both x0 and its partner, and keep whichever repaired packing has the larger radius sum. Both members of each pair cost one local solve, so the number of restarts per budget is halved. This doubles the diversity of the start set for the same random draws, since the partner has the same geometry seen from the other corner, and it is cheap to implement inside the restart loop. Keep all randomness drawn from rng.
backlog.title: Antithetic reflected starts

memo: Nothing beat the incumbent (-2.6280); noise sd is about 0.0023. Best results were rng.choice fix -2.6286 and mirror symmetry -2.6281, both noise. Worse: Sobol init -2.6268, annealing acceptance -2.6266, window re-optimization -2.6261, 40/60 basin-hopping split -2.6249, Lubachevsky-Stillinger growth -2.5956, log-barrier BFGS -1.1834 (keep SLSQP). Basin-hopping and restart-variant ideas did not help, so plain restarts are at least as good. The bigger problem was execution: many slots crashed or had patch failures or aborts. Next: make edits tiny and exact, and check that repair keeps the packing valid. Try small safe tweaks: SLSQP maxiter/ftol, better initial radii, analytic gradients (carefully), and a tight-tolerance final polish of the best packing. Replicate any apparent gain before accepting it.
